name: Saint Josephine Bakhita
history: Kidnapped as a child in Darfur and sold into slavery, she suffered years of cruelty before being brought to Italy, where she came to know Christ through the Canossian Sisters. Declared free by an Italian court, she was baptised, entered their order and spent some fifty years in quiet service. She is patron of Sudan and of the victims of human trafficking.
life: Born in Darfur around 1869, she was seized by slave traders at about the age of eight. The shock was such that she forgot her own name, and her captors called her Bakhita, which means fortunate. She was bought and sold several times and treated with great cruelty; one owner had her body cut with scores of patterns and rubbed with salt. Eventually an Italian consul bought her in Khartoum and took her to Italy, where she became nanny to a family near Venice. Left in the care of the Canossian Sisters, she came to know the God she had sensed as a child. When her mistress wished to take her back to Africa she refused, and in 1889 an Italian court ruled that she was free. She was baptised Josephine in 1890 and professed as a Canossian in 1896. At Schio she served as cook, sacristan and doorkeeper, much loved by all. She died in 1947 and was canonised in 2000.
prayerTo: Saint Josephine Bakhita, you were enslaved and wounded, and in Christ you found the Master who loved you and set you free. Pray for all who are trafficked, enslaved or exploited, and for those who work to free them. Pray for me, that I may know I am loved by God and forgive as you forgave. Amen.
penance: Today is the World Day of Prayer against Human Trafficking. Pray for its victims and give to a charity that helps them, or find out whether something you buy is made by forced labour.
meditation: Benedict XVI wrote that Bakhita came to know she was definitively loved, and that whatever happened, this Love was waiting for her. Do you believe that about yourself?
